text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Spanish painter FRANCESCO GOYA was born in 1746. He became famous for his paintings of the war against France in the early 1800's.

Russian goldsmith and jeweller PETER CARL FABERGE was born in 1846. He was popular with the European royalty and especially noted for his bejewelled Easter eggs. The sparkling eggs contained gifts and where made for the Tsars to give to their Tsarinas.
Dutch Post-Impressionist painter VINCENT VAN GOUGH was born in 1853. He only sold one painting during his life, but his works later fetched the highest prices paid in the art world.
American cartoon voice-over artist MEL BLANC, who became famous as the voices for Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck.

American jazz clarinettist BENNY GOODMAN, the 'King of Swing', was born in 1909. He was a songwriter and orchestra leader. He had his greatest commercial success with "Goody Goody" (1936), "The Glory Of Love" (1936), "Goodnight My Love" (1937) and "There'll Be Some Changes Made" (1941). The 1956 film "The BENNY GOODMAN Story" chronicled his life. He died in June 1986.
Australian artist PRO HART was born in 1928.
US singer, keyborard player, bass player and guitarist ROBERT TEPPER was born in 1958. His first hit "No Easy Way Out" (1986) was from the film "Rocky IV".
** EVENTS **
1431 : Condemned as a heretic by an English dominated
church court, JOAN of Arc was burnt at the stake at Rouen. She was canonised by Pope BENEDICT XV in 1920.
1498 : CHRISTOPHER COLUMBUS set sail with six ships from
Sanlucar in Spain on his third voyage of exploration to discover the South Americas.
1536 : In England, King HENRY VIII married his third
wife, JANE SEYMOUR, just 11 days after the execution of ANNE BOLEYN.
1778 : FRANCOIS MARIE AROUET, better known as VOLTAIRE,
French novelist, historian, playwright, and philosopher, regarded as the embodiment of 18th century enlightenment, died in Paris.
1840 : British dandy BEAU BRUMMELL died in a lunatic
asylum. Apart from wild clothing BRUMMELL is best remembered for asking an associate 'Who's your fat friend?' The friend was the Prince of Wales.
1856 : The Crimean War ended. The three-year struggle
ended as a victory for the British, and it's allied European powers, France, Austria, and Prussia. The war was best remembered for the infamous 'Charge of the Light Brigade'.
1867 : America bought Alaska from the Russians for 7.2
million dollars.
1911 : The first ever Indianapolis 500 motor race in the
United States was run and won by RAY HARROUN at an average speed of 74.59 miles per hour.
1921 : Australian won the 100th test against England by
10 wickets.
1925 : Radical educator RULDOLF STEINER died at the age
of 64. He rejected competitive education in favour of artistic pursuits.
1949 : In Britain a test pilot made the first escape by
ejector seat from a prototype "Flying Wing".
1959 : The first hovercraft was launched on the Isle of
Wight.
1959 : The Auckland Harbour Bridge on New Zealand's North
Island was officially opened.
1972 : Three Japanese Red Army terrorists gunned down 26

people at Tel Aviv's international airport. The three opened fire with automatic rifles on the crowds in the airport baggage hall. Two of the gunmen were shot and the third was arrested. They were reportedly working for a Palestinian group in Lebanon.
1980 : Twenty people were killed by Government troops
during the funeral of radical El Salvadorean churchman, OSCAR ROMERO.
1981 : US President RONALD REAGAN was seriously wounded

by a would-be assassin as he walked out of a Washington Hotel. The gunman, JOHN HINCKLEY JUNIOR fired six shots from a pistol. REAGAN's Press Secretary JIM BRADY was critically wounded in the head. HINCKLEY later confessed to the crime, saying he did it to impress actress JODY FOSTER.
1986 : American actor JAMES CAGNEY died at the age of 87.
1989 : Actor KURT RUSSELL stunned the world by proposing
to actress GOLDIE HORN. He popped the question in front of 1.8 billion people while the pair were presenting an award at the Oscars. She declined the offer.
1989 : Pro-democracy protestors in Beijing's Tiananmen

Square erected a 30 foot high Statue of Liberty. Just six days later the People's Libertion Army marched on the students and literally crushed the protest. More than 2,000 died and 10,000 were injured when the Chinese government ordered the crackdown.
1990 : France banned imports of British beef in case it
carried the BSE virus, known as "mad cow disease".
1992 : The United Nations Security Council voted to
impose sanctions against Serb-led Yugoslavia.
